features.title: Claude in Echo is told what the plugin gives: installed, its part is laid out in the data folder's .plugins/obsidian/ (finding a vault, asking Echo's index with the CLI there, adding notes, where the user manages it) and the core lists it with the manifest's summary

Each confirmed vault is an entry for Claude: a row in the core with its "when Claude looks here" line, its guide (name, folder, whom it is for, its description) in .plugins/obsidian/<vault>/; the summary names the vaults; a vault not yet confirmed has none
A vault's change reaches Claude at once: its "when" line, name or whom it is for edited, or the vault removed (its entry gone)
Knowledge is an entry for Claude while it is on and holds notes, first; turned off, the entry goes
A vault's description is the user's data to Claude: a hostile "when" line (a |, tags, a line break, an instruction) stays one row of the core and plain text in the guide
No runtime skill: the skill older versions gave (obsidian-vaults) is taken away and none is laid out

Claude in Echo may run the index's read commands without asking (uses.sessions.commands: search, info, links, backlinks, resolve, tags, where, tasks, unresolved — named on the install sheet, not rename_plan); they work from the laid-out launcher, also in a read-only routine
